## Summary

- migrate the installed Sepo runtime from v0.3.0 to `self-evolving/repo@v0.5.0` (`5f7d203`)
- update shared agent workflows, actions, prompts, docs, tests, and model defaults
- add the missing literature-template deployment actions/workflow, issue templates, and root agent guidance
- replace the obsolete `install-sepo.yml` issue form with the Markdown command template
- preserve target-only bug/feature templates and literature-specific runtime behavior

## Literature customizations preserved

The Sepo update was merged with the literature-template overlay rather than copied wholesale. In particular, this keeps:

- discussion creation returning both the GraphQL node ID and URL, as required by `publish-literature-update`
- preview/canonical deployment CLIs, helpers, and tests
- literature update parsing/publishing and its tests
- the `/chat` → `/answer` alias and `SEPO_SITE_BRANCH` implementation-base behavior
- site build validation in `test-scripts.yml`

This addresses the TypeScript incompatibility that caused run `29708524273` to conclude `verify_failed`.

## Infrastructure added

- Sepo v0.5 cache seeding and self-improvement workflows
- `deploy-sepo-site` and `resolve-discussion-ids` actions
- canonical site deployment workflow
- missing agent prompts and literature issue templates
- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`

## Validation

- `bash .agent/scripts/post-agent-verify.sh`
- `npm --prefix .agent test`
- `npm run check`
- `npm run build`
- `npm test` — 69 passed
- parsed every workflow, action manifest, and agent action template as YAML
- `git diff --check`

The existing `agent/memory` branch was left untouched. No `agent/rubrics` branch currently exists.

Closes #16

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #17 upgrades the installed Sepo runtime from v0.3.0 to v0.5.0 using an overlay merge strategy against the literature-template, preserving repo-specific customizations (deployment CLIs, `/answer` alias, `SEPO_SITE_BRANCH`, discussion `id`+`url` return). The update fixes a TypeScript incompatibility that caused run `29708524273` to conclude `verify_failed`. It adds three major capabilities — live-progress reporting, a self-improvement workflow, and GitHub attachment download — along with OIDC auth, actor-association logic, and infrastructure scaffolding (workflows, actions, agent prompts, issue templates). All 69 tests pass and explicit validation steps (build, type-check, YAML parse, `git diff --check`) were run by the author.

---

## Review

This is a thorough, well-structured runtime upgrade with comprehensive test coverage and careful preservation of literature-specific behavior. The design choices (self-improvement opt-in, progress policy defaults, triage default change) are sound and documented. One low-risk pagination gap warrants tracking before this runtime spreads to higher-volume repositories.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Issue list pagination gap | WARNING | `findExistingRunProposalIssue` fetches at most 100 issues with no page loop; in repos with >100 open issues a same-run proposal could be missed, creating a duplicate. |
| `/tmp` hardcoded fallback | INFO | `self-improvement.ts` uses `"/tmp"` as a string literal fallback while peer modules use `os.tmpdir()`; minor cross-platform inconsistency. |
| `AGENT_DISPLAY_MODEL` default flip | INFO | Default changed from `false` to `true`; existing deployed repos will now show provider/model/runner footers on agent responses where they previously didn't. |
| `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` not in diff | INFO | PR summary lists both as added infrastructure, but neither appears in the files list; worth confirming they are present on the branch. |
| No rubrics configured | INFO | `agent/rubrics` branch is uninitialized; rubric-based review returned N/A and will continue to do so until the rubrics bootstrap workflow is run. |

---

## Progress

- 69 tests passing; 16 new test files covering all major new modules (progress, self-improvement, attachment download, actor association, reactions, followup intent)
- `github-attachment-download.ts` security posture verified good: strict URL allowlist, content-length fast-fail + streaming size cap, `AbortController` kept alive through body read, SHA-256 deterministic filenames
- `acpx` wide semver range (`^0.6.1` → `^0.12.0`) mitigated by pinned lock file entry
- `sleepSync` with `Atomics.wait` confirmed as correct blocking-sleep pattern for sync CLIs on modern Node.js
- `discussion.ts` tightening (require both `id` and `url`) is correct and load-bearing for `publish-literature-update`
- Triage default change (`answer` for uncommanded mentions, `AGENT_TRIAGE_MODE=agent` to restore old behavior) documented in changelog, config list, and architecture diagrams
- Inline comment posted on `.agent/src/cli/apply-self-improvement-decision.ts:152` flagging the pagination gap

---

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Issue list pagination gap</summary>

**Cause:** `findExistingRunProposalIssue` calls `gh api --method GET repos/{repo}/issues -f per_page=100` with no `page` parameter loop. If the repo accumulates >100 total issues (open or closed, since `state=all`), the function can silently miss an existing proposal issue for the same run and create a duplicate.

**Candidate solutions:**
1. Replace the single `gh(...)` call with `gh(["api", "--paginate", ...])` and concatenate pages before filtering.
2. Add a label filter (`-f label=agent/self-improvement`) so the result set stays small without pagination; this requires the issue-creation path to attach that label.
3. Accept the risk for now with a code comment, given this repo's small issue volume, and track as a follow-up.

**Comments:** The claude reviewer rated this WARNING but still voted SHIP given the low practical risk for this specific repository.

</details>

<details>
<summary>`/tmp` hardcoded fallback</summary>

**Cause:** `writeTempMarkdownFile` in `self-improvement.ts` uses `process.env.RUNNER_TEMP || "/tmp"` with a string literal fallback. Other modules (`progress-cancel.ts`, `github-attachment-download.ts`) use `os.tmpdir()` for the same pattern.

**Candidate solutions:** Replace `"/tmp"` with `os.tmpdir()` for consistency. No behavior difference on GitHub Actions Linux runners.

</details>

<details>
<summary>`AGENT_DISPLAY_MODEL` default flip</summary>

**Cause:** The new `model-defaults.json` or runtime config changes `AGENT_DISPLAY_MODEL` from `false` to `true`. Any repo inheriting this runtime will begin showing provider/model/runner footers on all agent responses after merging.

**Candidate solutions:** Accept as intentional — the change is documented in the changelog and configuration list. Existing repos can opt out with `AGENT_DISPLAY_MODEL=false`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>`AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` not in diff</summary>

**Cause:** The PR body lists `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` as added infrastructure, but neither appears in the 97-file diff. They may be at the repo root (outside `.agent/`) and simply not captured in the files summary, or they may not have been committed.

**Candidate solutions:** Confirm these files exist on the PR branch with `gh api repos/self-evolving/literature-example-hcllms/contents/AGENTS.md?ref=dfdaf8d65e159ebf35a1cb4d78ff50852340f595`. If missing, add them.

</details>

---

## Recommended Next Step

**HUMAN_DECISION** — the one WARNING (pagination gap) requires a design choice between `--paginate` and a label-based filter before an automated fix-pr pass would be appropriate; all other findings are informational or require a maintainer acceptance call.

---

## Final Verdict

**MINOR_ISSUES**

---

## Action Items

- [ ] Fix `findExistingRunProposalIssue` in `.agent/src/cli/apply-self-improvement-decision.ts` to paginate or label-filter the issue list so runs in higher-volume repos cannot miss an existing proposal issue
- [ ] Confirm `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are present on the PR branch; add them if missing
- [ ] (Optional) Replace `"/tmp"` literal with `os.tmpdir()` in `self-improvement.ts:writeTempMarkdownFile` for consistency with peer modules

## Rubrics Update

No changes were committed to [`agent/rubrics`](https://github.com/self-evolving/literature-example-hcllms/tree/agent/rubrics) from PR #17.

I've reviewed the full PR conversation. Here's my assessment:

**PR #17** is a Sepo v0.3→v0.5 infrastructure migration. Analyzing the conversation for durable, trusted-contributor preferences:

- **lolipopshock** (Shannon Shen), the PR author and `Requested by` actor, has `author_association: CONTRIBUTOR`. Their only comment is `@sepo-agent /review` — a one-off command invocation, not an explicit request to add/update a rubric and not a durable preference statement.
- **All other content** (the review synthesis, the pagination-gap WARNING, the inline comment) comes from `github-actions[bot]` with `author_association: NONE`. Per the instructions, bot/agent-authored feedback is advisory only and cannot become a user/team preference unless a trusted contributor explicitly endorses it. No trusted contributor endorsed any of it.
- No `agent/rubrics` branch exists yet, and no existing `/rubrics/` to update.

There is no repeated reviewer feedback, no explicit human preference about style/workflow/communication, and no durable "future agents should…" instruction from a trusted contributor. The single WARNING (issue-list pagination gap) is a one-off code observation from a bot, not a stable user/team preference.

**no rubric changes**
